name: Parakrama Samudra (Sea of Parakrama)
description: Colossal shallow reservoir consisting of five separate ancient lakes interconnected by relief channels, serving as the lifeblood of Polonnaruwa agriculture.
historical_significance: One of the greatest engineering feats of ancient Sri Lanka, famously declaring that not a drop of water from rain should reach the ocean without serving mankind.

name: Kala Wewa & Balalu Wewa
description: Massive twin reservoir feeding the 87km ancient Yoda Ela canal with a slope of just 6 inches per mile, supplying water to Anuradhapura.
historical_significance: Features the colossal Avukana Buddha statue carved directly out of a granite cliff face near its spillway.

name: Minneriya Reservoir (Minneri Deviyo)
description: Vast ancient reservoir whose receding waters during the dry season create lush grass plains that host 'The Gathering', the largest congregation of Asian elephants in the world.
historical_significance: King Mahasen was deified as 'Minneri Deviyo' (God of Minneriya) by grateful farmers for constructing this irrigation wonder.

name: Sorabora Wewa Natural Sluice Tank
constructed_by: Bulata the Giant (King Dutugemunu era - 2nd Century BC)
description: Unique ancient reservoir where the sluice gate (Bisokotuwa) was carved directly out of a solid living granite bedrock rather than constructed with dressed stones.
historical_significance: Built by a local villagers' leader Bulata while supplying food to King Dutugemunu's army.
best_viewpoint: Granite sluice gate viewpoint at dawn
